sources.name: ExRx (current 2020s tables, ages 18-39)
sources.population: ExRx performance standards for adults 18-39 (not population norms per ExRx); below-parallel squat
sources.notes: Snippet-only; summarizer often could not tell men's from women's table. Male 181 row also appeared as 100/190/230/320/415 in another snippet (likely the 148 row mis-attributed). Female untrained/novice column confirmed separately for 97-198 lb: 97:40/85, 105:50/90, 114:55/100, 123:55/105, 132:60/110, 148:65/120, 165:70/130, 181:75/140, 198:80/150, 199+:85/160. '199' key = 199+ class. These are the newer ExRx tables (with World Record column), much lower than the classic Kilgore/Rippetoe 2006 numbers. ExRx tiers are ~35-50% below Strength Level at Novice-Elite for women and ~10-20% below for men.

sources.notes: Gym-based table = flat BW multiples 0.75/1.0/1.25/1.65/2.0x. Much lower than Strength Level at Novice+ (SL 120 lb male: 92/136/192/257/327).

Squat.summary: Strength Level rows re-verified (male 120, female 120 match). ExRx (new tables), FitnessVolt and StrengthLog all sit below SL at Intermediate (roughly 10-25% for men; ExRx women ~40% lower), so SL is the most generous-to-strong / hardest standard; no source suggests SL is too easy.

Front Squat.summary: SL front squat essentially confirmed (current site ~1-2% higher for light men). FitnessVolt's 180-lb Intermediate/Advanced (239/306) is within ~3% of the app's SL row.

Leg Press.summary: Strength Level sled leg press rows re-verified exactly. No independent bodyweight table found (Marathon Handbook only re-cites SL; there are no official leg press norms). Machine type matters a lot (horizontal press ~15-20% lower).
